newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JULY 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JULY 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Chamber of Mines and the National Union of Mineworkers have agreed to productivity-linked wage increases, the first such deal in the gold mining industry.

- Some confidence returned to South Africa's financial markets on Monday after the gold price held above the $320 an ounce level, but analysts were reluctant to predict either direction or trading range.
- South Korean car manufacturer Daewoo would make a decision on setting up a car plant in South Africa within eight weeks, public relations officer Nick Bates said.

- The Mpumalanga Parks Board's contentious 788 million rand game parks deal with Dubai-based Dolphin Group has been put at risk by a proposed 77 percent cut in the board's yearly budget to 11 million rand from about 53 million.

- The corruption of the criminal justice system by domestic and international organised crime could lead to a collapse of South Africa's democratic system and negatively affect economic growth if not stopped soon, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said.
- Gold producers in South Africa and Australia were desperately trying to lock in the present gold price by hedging and selling gold forward, traders said.
- Some of the assets of wine cooperative KWV were of "public nature", according to a forensic audit of the the wine and spirits cooperative.

- Chemical Services continued its strategy of growth through acquisition to post a 22 percent rise in turnover to 595 million rand and a 22 percent rise in earnings to 41 cents a share for the half year to June 30.

- The gold price rose in London by more than $2 an ounce on Monday, fixing at $321.70 from $319.50 on Friday, but dealers said the rise was only a technical correction and did not indicate the start of a recovery.

- The national executive committee of the Afriacan National Congress warned business and labour that they had to resolve their differences over proposed new laws governing basic conditions of service or the legislation would be withdrawn.
- Security elements from the former government were involved in organised crime syndicates which had the capacity to bring down the criminal justice system, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said.
